text: Bamman and colleagues (7) categorized a group of young and old men and women based on their response to 16 weeks of multiset progressive lower-body resistance exercise: The top quartile increased muscle cross-sectional area by 58%, and the bottom quartile showed no mean gains; the balance of the group showed a moderate response with an increase of 28%. These findings have led to classifying subjects as responders and nonresponders to resistance exercise, thereby highlighting the role of genetics in muscle development.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 7: Factors in Maximal Hypertrophic Development
